title: Stress harness: kernel compatibility ablation and prompt-set diffs
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the stress harness run and ablation notes we used to triage a quality/perf regression observed after merging the new flash-attn kernel + paged-KV adapt + continuous-batching defaults. The goal is to give a reproducible playbook, concrete diffs on our prompt sets, token-level latency distributions, and prioritized next actions for runtime and model teams.

Summary (TL;DR):
- After the kernel change deployed to staging on 2026-02-15 (serving-runtime@sha: abc123 -> PR#5123), we observed a small but consistent quality drop on a subset of prompt sets (mainly long-context instruction-following and code-completion edges) and occasional token-latency spikes for short-turns under cont-batch.
- Latency: median token latency improved ~12% for long sequences (seq>=1024), but p95 increased by ~8% on short-turn (<64 tokens) with cont-batching enabled in the pipeline. P99 shows a fat tail in some cases.
- Quality: automated eval metrics show a 2.5% relative decrease in pass-rate on the Long Instruction prompt-set (see metrics below). Manual diff shows hallucination increase on certain retrieval-style prompts where KV eviction interacts with flash attention fused chunks.
- Hypothesis: kernel changes improved steady-state throughput for long sequences but introduced subtle ordering/attention window alignment differences when paged-KV page boundaries occur at specific token offsets combined with cont-batching re-ordering. These manifest as small attention weight shifts and downstream decoding divergences.

Test harness and environment:
- Baseline runtime: serving-runtime v0.73.4 (kernel: flash-attn-v1, kv: paged-kv-legacy, cont-batch: disabled)
- Candidate runtime: serving-runtime v0.74.0-rc (kernel: flash-attn-v2, kv: paged-kv-rolling, cont-batch: enabled with default policy)
- Hardware: dedicated A100-s XM nodes (8x40GB) with CUDA 12.2, cuBLASLT, Triton 2.9.
- Model: open-llama-13b-finetuned (quantized int8 profile q-int8-ld) — same model binary pinned for both runs.
- Dataset/prompt sets used (short descriptions):
  - stress-long-instr: 3k prompts, long instruction + multi-step constraints (avg ctx 1800 tokens).
  - stress-short-turns: 5k prompts, many short requests (<=32 tokens) hitting cont-batching hot path.
  - stress-retrieval-qa: 2k prompts, retrieval context + citation-checks where exact grounding is required.
  - stress-code-edgecases: 1.2k prompts, code completion with unusual braces/indentation and tokenization boundaries.

Key numeric diffs (candidate vs baseline):
- stress-long-instr (n=3000): pass-rate 0.73 -> 0.712 (-2.5% relative); median latency per token 24.8ms -> 21.8ms (-12%); p95 token latency 68ms -> 62ms (-8.8%).
- stress-short-turns (n=5000): median request latency 42ms -> 38ms (-9.5%); token-level p95 9ms -> 12.2ms (+35%); p99 18ms -> 34ms (+89%).
- stress-retrieval-qa (n=2000): exact-match 0.61 -> 0.58 (-4.9% relative); hallucination rate (model asserts unsupported fact) 0.043 -> 0.066 (+53%).
- stress-code-edgecases (n=1200): BLEU-like code-match 0.68 -> 0.67 (-1.5%); notable divergence cases clustered around tokenization page boundaries.

Representative manual diffs (short excerpts):
- Prompt (retrieval-qa): "Given the excerpt below, list the three policies cited explicitly."
  - Baseline output: lists the three policy names, includes exact phrase matches from context.
  - Candidate output: gives two correct names, then fabricates a third that is semantically plausible but not present in context.
  - Notes: hallucination appears when the model attends to a buffered KV page that is partially stale due to page roll; topology suggests a missed explicit copy of the final context tokens into the active KV window.

- Prompt (code-edgecase): auto-complete function with long docstring where docstring length crosses a page boundary.
  - Baseline: completes valid code with correct closing braces.
  - Candidate: produces an extra closing brace in ~7% of runs for this prompt (deterministic seed fixed).
  - Notes: likely alignment/stride effect when attention chunks align differently under fused flash kernels.

Investigation steps we ran:
1) Deterministic replay: replayed 100 failing prompts with rng fixed and KV logging enabled (kv-page checksums + offsets). Observed page checksum mismatch between baseline and candidate at token index ~1376 for a subset of runs.
2) Isolated cont-batch: disabled continuous-batching on the candidate build; re-run short-turn suite -> p99 back to baseline levels, hallucination unchanged for long prompts. Implication: cont-batch exacerbates latency tail but not primary cause of hallucination.
3) Kernel ablation: built candidate with flash-attn-v2 disabled (fallback to v1) but kept paged-kv-rolling and cont-batch -> long-instr pass-rate returned to baseline. Strong signal that flash-attn-v2 fusion changes are correlated with quality deltas.
4) KV page size sweep: varied page size from 4k to 16k tokens and observed hallucination rate scale with smaller page sizes.
5) Token alignment test: instrumented attention heads to dump per-head attention mass on tokens crossing page boundaries. Noted small but deterministic redistribution in heads 8 and 10 under v2 kernel.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1 (high confidence): flash-attn-v2's fused chunking/striding introduces micro-reorder in attention computation when paged-KV page boundary occurs exactly at a chunk edge. This changes attention weights subtly and cascades into decoding differences for brittle prompts.
- H2 (medium confidence): cont-batching re-ordering increases exposure to buffered KV pages that are near eviction, amplifying p99 latency and occasionally causing partial page reads.
- H3 (low confidence): quantization rounding behavior interacts with new kernel math path, increasing numerical noise for borderline tokens.

Short-term mitigations executed:
- Rollback plan: keep candidate in canary with traffic cap 10% and route critical customers to baseline for now.
- Hotfix PR: temporarily disable flash-attn-v2 fusion for sequences with page boundary alignment (patch gating in kernel selector). PR linked above (#5123) contains a toggle.
- Cont-batch tweak: reduce cont-batch max-batch-window from default 80ms -> 35ms for staging to reduce p99 tail; observed immediate p99 improvement on short-turn suite.

Repro recipe (minimal):
1) Checkout serving-runtime@candidate-abc123 and baseline tag.
2) Use quantized model binary pinned to q-int8-ld path /models/open-llama-13b/v2/q-int8-ld.bin (ensure same file for both runs).
3) Run the harness: "./tools/stress_runner --suite stress-retrieval-qa --concurrency 8 --log-kv-pages --seed 42 --suppress-rng-skips"
4) Collect artifacts: token-latency.csv, kv-page-checksums.log, attention-dumps.tar.gz, model-decoding-diffs.json
5) Compare with the script tools/diff_eval.py which outputs per-prompt pass/fail and a side-by-side token diff.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are there other models (larger or different architectures) exhibiting the same sensitivity? We observed smaller signal on 7b family; need to expand sample.
- Does enabling a small overlap window when paging (copy last N tokens into next page) mitigate without heavy perf regression?
- Can we design a regression test that is cheap to run on PRs that would have caught this — likely a targeted prompt-set exercising page boundaries and fused chunking.

Proposed next steps (owners):
- eng-applied-ml (Aisha, Jonah): create a compact regression suite (200 prompts) focusing on page-boundary edge-cases and add as pr-check-integration. ETA: 2026-03-10.
- serving-runtime (Luca): add a kernel-selector guard that disables v2 fusion when model ctx length > page_size - overlap_threshold. Short-term patch by 2026-03-08.
- infra/sre (Priya): keep canary routing cap at 10% until a full mitigation verified; instrument additional metric for kv-page-read-latency.
- research (TBD): run numerical sensitivity tests to evaluate quantization math path differences.

Quick notes to reviewers:
- This doc mixes noisy manual diffs and structured measurements; use the linked artifacts to reproduce exact runs.
- Avoid broad disabling of paged-KV unless we can show throughput loss >8% on long sequences — paged-KV is critical for our cost targets.
- We should treat this as a kernel-edge quality-sensitivity class of issues; long-term fix may require explicit attention alignment invariants in fused kernels.

Appendix: useful commands and artifact locations
- Re-run full suite: ./tools/full_eval --suites stress-* --nodes 4 --save-artifacts /tmp/harness_run_$(date +%s)
- Artifact S3 path (staging): s3://redwood-evals/stress-harness/2026-02-18-candidate-abc123/
- KV logging flags: --log-kv-pages --kv-page-size=8192 --kv-overlap=64

Notes to self (informal):
- Some prompts are brittle because the eval scoring is strict (exact-match). For customer-facing impact we should also compute fuzzy-match and human-review for highest-severity diffs.
- If we add pr-checks, keep them cheap; consider sampling 50 prompts and compute a quick-pass metric (delta >1.5% flags).

End of doc.
